items.headline: OpenAI revenue miss triggers a broad semiconductor selloff
items.why: A roughly $20B gap between OpenAI's actual annualized run-rate (near $50B) and the market's assumed figure (about $70B) knocked the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index down 3.4% in a day and cut Intel, Micron, Broadcom and Nvidia between 3% and 5%, showing how much of the sector's valuation now rests on one company's growth story.

sources.title: Chip Stocks Drop as OpenAI Revenue Falls Short of Expectations

items.headline: TSMC heads into a sixth straight record profit quarter
items.why: Record revenue and a raised full-year growth outlook, driven by 3nm and advanced-packaging demand, confirm AI chip demand is still outrunning supply even as the broader chip tape wobbled on OpenAI's numbers the same week.

sources.title: TSMC to get 6th straight record profit quarter

items.headline: Analysts expect AI to drive roughly two-thirds of S&P 500 earnings growth this quarter
items.why: With semiconductor earnings alone projected up 136% for Q3, the index's earnings season now hinges almost entirely on AI-linked names delivering, which raises the stakes of any single disappointment over the next two weeks.

sources.title: AI Companies Expected to Drive 31% Uptick in Q3 Earnings

items.headline: Bitcoin and ether both lower on the week as Treasury yields hit historic highs
items.why: Rising yields are pulling speculative capital toward cash and bonds, and the pressure is showing up beyond the coins themselves in weekly declines for crypto-linked equities.

sources.title: Bitcoin and ethereum prices today, Monday, October 12, 2026: How bond yields 'threaten' crypto prices

items.headline: Crypto fell to a two-week low as an oil-driven inflation scare hit risk assets
items.why: Bitcoin and ether opened at their weakest levels in weeks the same day Brent spiked on Strait of Hormuz attacks, a reminder that crypto is currently trading as a leveraged risk asset, not an inflation hedge.

sources.title: Bitcoin and ethereum prices today, Thursday, October 8, 2026: Crypto values fall as oil prices soar

items.headline: Fed skips October after a unanimous September hike to 3.75%-4.00%
items.why: Market odds of an October move collapsed from 70% to under 20% in two weeks, but the minutes show nearly every policymaker still expects one more hike by year-end — this is a live hiking cycle, not a pause ahead of cuts.

sources.title: Federal Reserve: more hikes ahead after October pause - UOB

items.headline: Tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz hit their highest weekly pace since the Iran war began
items.why: At least a dozen attacks on oil, LNG and LPG tankers in a single week sets a new escalation baseline and is the direct mechanism behind this month's crude risk premium.

sources.title: Attacks on tankers in Hormuz hit highest of any week since start of Iran war, sources say

items.headline: Broadcom and SpaceX turn to private lenders for AI chip financing
items.why: Deals reportedly north of $50B and $40B routed through private credit rather than bank balance sheets signal the AI buildout is starting to strain conventional financing, pushing the risk into less-regulated lenders.

items.headline: Gold slides to around $4,200 as the dollar strengthens
items.why: The pullback from September's highs above $4,400 is the first real test of whether 2026's gold rally was driven by safe-haven demand or by a weak dollar that is now reversing.

sources.title: Gold price today, Tuesday, October 13, 2026: Lower gold prices could be the next buying opportunity

items.headline: Brent crude near $106, up roughly 61% year-over-year
items.why: Oil costing well over half as much again as a year ago feeds straight into the inflation data the Fed is watching, reinforcing the case policymakers cite for another hike.

sources.title: Current price of oil as of October 9, 2026

items.headline: Copper slips below $40.50 with no clear catalyst as CPI looms
items.why: Unexplained, sector-specific selling in a bellwether industrial metal often front-runs a macro data surprise, and the next US CPI print is the test traders are now watching for.

sources.title: Copper Fund Slips 0.44% to US$40.45 as Miners Fall

items.headline: S&P 500 pinned inside a wedge under 7,820 resistance
items.why: The index has not broken either boundary, so the next directional signal is purely mechanical: a close above 7,820 or below the wedge's lower line, not a forecast of which way it goes.

items.headline: Nasdaq 100 back to neutral after 16 sessions as the chip index drags
items.why: Its ascending channel broke and stopped out the prior bullish read; the semiconductor index is now acting as a brake on the broader tech-heavy benchmark rather than a tailwind.

items.headline: Brent crude holds above its post-September-30 uptrend, resistance near 111
items.why: This ties directly to the Hormuz-driven rally: the trendline from the late-September lows is the level that would need to break to signal the geopolitical risk premium is fading.

items.headline: Gold's chart structure points to a 3,970 downside level
items.why: The technical picture lines up with the fundamental story of a stronger dollar and higher yields, giving traders a specific level to watch for confirmation either way.

items.headline: US 10-year yield testing its short-term uptrend, with 5.16% the level that matters
items.why: A close below 5.16% would form a possible double top, which would be the first technical crack in the rising-yield narrative that has been pressuring both the dollar-sensitive metals and crypto.
